folders.text:
Fiu turns real code from a repository into small Verified Workouts (Drills, Katas, Predictions, Diagnoses) that keep people fluent in code they didn't write.
src: the TypeScript CLI, one folder per concern: generation and the Verified Gate, the sandbox, training, the Atlas, Tracks, the map, sharing, background generation, and agent mode.
test: the node --test suite covering each of those areas, with a mock model in place of a real provider.
docs/adr: the architecture decisions; SPEC.md and GLOSSARY.md hold the specification and the domain terms.

src.text: Fiu's source: the CLI entry point and configuration, with one folder per concern from generating and verifying Workouts to the Atlas, Tracks, sharing, and agent mode.

src/agent.text: Agent mode: lets a coding agent such as Claude Code generate Workouts, Tracks, and the Atlas through Fiu's MCP server, and installs the skill and slash commands that drive it.

src/atlas.text: The Atlas: Fiu's map of what each folder, file, and key function is for, with computed links, search, business rules, and the Understand-Anything overlay.

src/background.text: Background generation: the post-commit hook behind `fiu auto`, and the refill that turns each commit into a queued Quick Drill or rule check within consent and caps.

src/commands.text: The CLI's command handlers: generating Workouts, exploring modules and flows into Tracks, training, the Atlas, costs, and workspace setup.

src/cost.text: Generation cost: per-model token prices and the arithmetic that turns token usage into the dollar amounts Fiu estimates and reports.

src/explore.text: Tracks: choosing 3 to 5 files of a module or business flow worth practising, planning their order and kinds with the model, and storing Track progress.

src/languages.text: Language Profiles: the data that tells Fiu how to build, test, and parse results for each language, plus the built-in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Go ones.

src/map.text: The comprehension map and statistics: which files and business flows have been practised, which are risky or out of date, rule check results, and what to practise next.

src/runner.text: The training runner: drives an Attempt, re-running tests on each save, serving hints, recording answers and outcomes, and running the user's own command alongside.

src/sandbox.text: The OS sandbox every piece of Workout code runs in: no network, no secrets, no writes outside scratch space, resource limits, and a canary that proves the isolation holds.

src/sharing.text: Team sharing: publishes Workouts, Tracks, and the Atlas to the fiu/workouts branch with git plumbing, and fetches teammates' Workouts, re-verifying them in the sandbox.

src/synthesis.text: Workout generation: prompts the model for a Drill, Kata, Prediction, Series, or Diagnosis, checks its answer's shape, verifies it in the sandbox, and retries with feedback.

src/verify.text: The Verified Gate: runs every generated Workout's tests in the sandbox to prove its answer and each Variant, and spots generated bugs that already exist in the real source.

src/workouts.text: Workouts and Attempts on disk: saving Verified Workouts with their README, opening Attempts, the queue, rule check results, and the Debrief shown after each Workout.

test.text: Fiu's test suite (node --test): one file per area, from generation and the Verified Gate to the sandbox, sharing, and the Atlas, with a mock model and shared helpers.

src/agent/drills.ts.text: Agent mode's engine: prepares requests for Drills, Katas, Predictions, Diagnoses, Tracks, and Atlas folders, then checks, verifies, and saves what the coding agent submits.

functions.AgentDrills.prepareTrack: Starts a Track over a module directory or a business flow: checks the module, shortlists enough candidate files with their Atlas notes, and returns the Track's rules and kinds.

src/agent/mcp.ts.text: The fiu MCP server: registers the tools a coding agent calls (prepare/submit Drills, Tracks, rules, Atlas, search) and turns their results or expected errors into tool replies.

functions.respond: Wraps a tool's work as a JSON text reply, turning agent-facing errors into error replies the agent can read and rethrowing anything unexpected.
functions.staleInstallNotice: Warns when the Fiu skill installed for the agent is older than the running Fiu, telling the user to reinstall it.
functions.createMcpServer: Builds the MCP server and registers every Fiu tool with its description and input schema, delegating each to agent mode.

src/agent/texts.ts.text: The text Fiu installs into a coding agent: the Fiu skill's instructions, the /fiu-drill and /fiu-atlas commands, and the optional end-of-task block, each stamped with Fiu's version.

functions.skillMarkdown: The Fiu skill: how the agent chooses targets, delegates generation of Workouts, Tracks, and the Atlas to a subagent, reports outcomes, and coaches without giving answers away.
functions.atlasCommandMarkdown: The /fiu-atlas slash command, which asks the skill to build the Atlas for a named folder or the whole repository.
functions.commandMarkdown: The /fiu-drill slash command, which asks the skill to create a Workout for a file, symbol, or learning goal.
functions.afterTasksBlock: The CLAUDE.md block asking the agent to create a quick Drill from the file it changed most after each coding task that changed logic.

src/atlas/rules.ts.text: Business rules Fiu can check: reads them from .fiu-rules.md and Understand-Anything's domain graph, finds a rule from the user's words, and locates the functions that should enforce it.

functions.locateRule: Finds where a rule should be enforced: its pinned function, functions or constants the rule names, or else Atlas search results sharing several of the rule's words.
functions.readRules: Collects the repository's business rules: the team's .fiu-rules.md first, then Understand-Anything's rules not already listed there.
functions.findRule: Picks the one rule the user means by exact text or by matching all their words, otherwise explains whether none or several rules match and lists some.
functions.parseRulesFile: Reads .fiu-rules.md: headings become domains, list items become rules, and an arrow pins a rule to a file or file#function.

src/atlas/search.ts.text: Finds the files and functions behind a learning goal by matching its words against paths, symbol names, Atlas text, and Understand-Anything tags, rarer words weighing more.

functions.searchAtlas: Scores every described file and function against the goal and ranks them by score, then callability, practice state, and whether the Atlas describes them.
functions.sameWord: Treats two words as the same when equal or when the shorter is a long enough prefix of the other, so related word forms match.
functions.stem: Strips common English endings (plurals, -ing, -ed) so different forms of a word compare equal.
functions.words: Splits text into meaningful search words: breaks camelCase, lowercases, drops short words and stopwords, and stems the rest.

src/atlas/symbols.ts.text: Finds the declarations in a source file and their line ranges without a parser, and picks the key functions worth describing by their branching density and size.

functions.endOf: Works out where a declaration ends: by balancing braces for brace languages, at a terminating semicolon, or by indentation for colon-and-indent languages.
functions.extractSymbols: Lists a file's top-level functions, classes, and methods with line ranges and a complexity score, skipping functions nested inside other functions.
functions.keyFunctions: Chooses a file's key functions: callable, not constructors, long enough, ranked by complexity score and length.

src/atlas/ua.ts.text: Reads an Understand-Anything graph (.understand-anything/ or .ua/) as foreign orientation: file and symbol summaries, layers, tour, business flows and their rules, and which are current.

functions.resolveFlows: Turns the domain graph into business flows with their domain, entry point, and ordered steps, each step mapped to a file and marked current when unchanged.
functions.resolveRules: Collects the business rules attached to domains, flows, and steps, with the domain, flow, and files each rule concerns.
functions.firstSentence: Shortens a summary to its first sentence, cutting at a clause or word boundary with an ellipsis when it is still too long.
functions.symbolOf: Matches a graph node to a symbol in the file, by full name or unique last name part, preferring symbols of the same kind.
functions.flowsThrough: Lists the business flows that pass through a file, marking whether a current step overlaps the given code or only the file.

src/background/auto.ts.text: Turns background generation on and off: asks consent with the cost and limits, records the setting, and installs, migrates, or removes Fiu's block in the git post-commit hook.

functions.removeHook: Removes Fiu's block from the post-commit hook, deleting the hook file when Fiu created it and nothing else remains.
functions.migrateLegacyHook: Replaces a hook block written under Fiu's former names (Fiutsu, Kintsugi) with the current one, unless hooks live in a custom hooksPath.
functions.enableAuto: Turns on background generation: unless pre-approved, shows what will be sent, the caps, and average spend and asks consent, then records it and installs the hook.
functions.installHook: Adds Fiu's block to the post-commit hook, creating an executable hook if needed, or returns the snippet to add by hand when core.hooksPath is set.
functions.autoCaps: The background limits in effect: queue cap, daily generation limit, AI-only commits, and expiry days, from the repository config or defaults.

src/background/refill.ts.text: Turns a commit into a queued Workout: checks consent and API key, takes a lock or defers to a backlog, expires stale Drills, and generates a Drill or rule check per commit.

functions.refill: Processes a commit (and in the background any backlog) into a Quick Drill or rule check, logging each outcome: skipped, deferred, failed, or saved.
functions.acquireLock: Takes the refill lock so only one generator runs, reclaiming a lock left by a dead or long-stale process.
functions.expireStaleWorkouts: Discards the user's own background Drills left untouched past the expiry age, never a teammate's shared ones.
functions.backgroundRefusal: Says why background generation must not run: it is switched off, or there is no consent to send code to the configured provider.
functions.resolveCommit: Resolves a revision such as HEAD to a full commit hash, failing when it names no commit in the repository.

src/cli.ts.text: The `fiu` command line: declares every command and flag, validates options, and wires each command to its handler with terminal output, prompts, and exit codes.

functions.positive: Reads a flag that must be a whole number of at least 1, rejecting anything else with a clear message.
functions.quickWhileCommand: `fiu quick --while`: offers Quick Workouts while the user's command runs, or just runs the command when there is no terminal, workspace, or ready Workout.
functions.runRefill: `fiu refill`: silently in the background from the hook, or interactively reporting each commit's outcome and offering to train the Workout it saved.
functions.trackKindList: Parses --kinds into the Workout kinds a Track may use, rejecting unknown ones.
functions.questionCount: Parses --questions: how many Predictions a Series asks, within the allowed range.

src/commands/drill.ts.text: `fiu drill`, `kata`, `predict`, and `diagnose`: resolves the target (a file, a folder, a What-if, or a business rule), checks key, sandbox, and consent, then generates the Workout.

functions.closestTo: For a What-if without a file, finds the best Atlas match for the user's sentence and asks them to confirm modelling the change there.
functions.ruleTarget: Resolves a rule check: finds the rule (or takes the user's words as one) and locates the function enforcing it, asking the user to confirm the place.
functions.directoryTarget: Recognises a folder target for a Prediction or Diagnosis, refusing folders outside the repository or inside the Fiu workspace.
functions.drill: Generates one Workout of any kind: picks the target, fails early on a missing API key, checks the sandbox and toolchain, asks consent to send code, then generates.
functions.pickUnpractised: Picks the first file in a folder worth asking about that the user has not practised yet.

src/commands/explore.ts.text: `fiu explore`: builds a Track of 3 to 5 Workouts over a module, the module closest to a goal, or an Understand-Anything business flow, with a cost estimate and fallbacks.

functions.explore: Starts a Track for a module, a goal, or a flow: resolves the module, requires an API key, and gathers enough candidate files with their Atlas notes.
functions.buildTrack: Asks consent, lets the model plan the steps, confirms them with an estimated cost, then generates each step, falling back to alternate files when one can't be Verified.
functions.exploreFlow: Builds a Track that follows a named business flow, its steps in the flow's order, when enough of its files can be drilled.
functions.moduleAbout: Chooses the module for a learning goal: the folder holding the best Atlas search results, widened to a parent until it has enough files for a Track.
functions.listFlows: Lists the Understand-Anything business flows that pass through enough files to make a Track.

src/commands/track.ts.text: `fiu track`: lists Tracks with their progress and continues one by training its next unfinished step.

functions.continueTrack: Shows a Track's progress and trains its next step, or reports the Track complete.
functions.trackListing: Lists every Track with how many of its steps have been attempted.
functions.formatProgress: Writes a Track's progress: its module or flow, steps done, and each step's mark, kind, file, and why, pointing at the next one.

src/commands/train.ts.text: `fiu train` and `fiu quick --while`: runs an Attempt at a Workout, from the watch-and-test loop for Drills and Katas to answering Predictions and Diagnoses, then the Debrief.

functions.train: Opens an Attempt at the chosen or pending Workout: Predictions and Diagnoses are answered in the terminal (a Series offers its next question), Drills and Katas run tests in the sandbox.
functions.quickWhile: Runs the user's command in the background and offers Quick Workouts until it finishes, then waits for it, never letting a Fiu failure cost the command.
functions.readKeys: Handles keys during a Drill or Kata: hints, giving up to see the Reference Solution, the background command's status, and quitting.
functions.readAnswer: Reads the user's choice for a Prediction or Diagnosis and how sure they were, reporting the background command if it finishes meanwhile.
functions.closeAttempt: Ends an Attempt: reveals an injected bug that may also exist in the real source, shows the Debrief, asks for a rating, and records the outcome.

src/config.ts.text: Fiu's settings: the repository's .fiu/config.json and the user's own config, validated, merged with defaults, and kept free of API keys inside the repository.

functions.resolveConfig: Merges repository and user settings over the defaults: provider, model, Language Profiles, prices, Workout kinds, Series length, and context.
functions.loadRepoConfig: Reads the repository's config, refusing API keys there because it lives inside the repository.
functions.readJson: Reads a JSON settings file, treating a missing file as no settings and reporting invalid JSON by path.
functions.parse: Validates settings against their schema, reporting every problem with the file's path.
functions.loadUserConfig: Reads the user's own config from their home config directory, where API keys may live.

src/explore/flows.ts.text: Business flows as Track sources: reads Understand-Anything's flows, finds the one the user names, and turns its files into Track candidates in the flow's order.

functions.findFlow: Finds the flow the user means by exact name or by all their words, otherwise lists the matching flows or all of them.
functions.readFlows: Reads the repository's Understand-Anything flows, explaining how to produce them when the integration is off or none exist.
functions.flowModule: The deepest folder shared by all of a flow's files, used as the Track's module.
functions.flowCandidates: Turns each drillable file a flow passes through into a candidate, noting which of the flow's steps it runs.

src/explore/plan.ts.text: Plans a Track with the model: presents the candidate files, asks for ordered steps with kinds and why lines plus alternates, and checks the plan against the rules.

functions.checkPlan: Lists what is wrong with a plan: step count, unknown or repeated files, empty why lines, disallowed kinds, a broken flow order, or a single kind used throughout.
functions.candidatesPrompt: Describes the module or flow and each candidate file with its size, flow steps, and Atlas notes or declarations for the planner.
functions.withAtlas: Attaches each candidate's Atlas description and key function notes, so the planner reads what files are for instead of their declarations.
functions.planTrack: Asks the model for a Track plan, sending back the problems once for a corrected plan, and returns the plan or its problems with the token usage.
functions.flowRules: Adapts the Track planning rules to a business flow: steps follow the flow's order and each why says what the file does in the flow.

src/explore/shortlist.ts.text: Shortlists the files of a module worth practising: tracked, drillable, of a workable size, ranked by how much branching logic they hold.

functions.candidateFor: Makes a file a Track candidate when it is drillable, in a supported language, and of workable size, with its logic score and a short outline of declarations.
functions.shortlist: Lists the git-tracked files of a module directory as candidates, richest logic first, capped at the shortlist size.
functions.logicScore: Scores a file's logic density from its branches per line, weighted by size; files too short or too long don't qualify.

src/explore/tracks.ts.text: Stores Tracks in the workspace: saving and loading them, giving each a dated id, and working out each step's status and the next one to train.

functions.trackProgress: Each step's status from its Workout, and the next step to train: one in progress first, else the first queued.
functions.listTracks: Reads every saved Track, newest first.
functions.loadTrack: Loads one Track by id, failing when there is none.
functions.trackId: A unique id for a new Track from the date and its module or flow name, numbered when the name is already taken.

src/map/flows.ts.text: `fiu map --flows`: practice coverage by Understand-Anything domain and business flow, each rule's measured status, and suggestions for what to check or explore next.

functions.buildFlowMap: Groups flows and rules by domain with each flow's practised files and each rule's status (follows, breaks, stale, waiting, unchecked), then suggests next steps.
functions.renderFlowMap: Writes the flow map as terminal text: a legend, each domain's rule tally and flows with file marks, the rules worth a look, and the suggestions.

src/map/map.ts.text: `fiu map`: colours every source file by practice state (complex and unpractised, out of date or AI-changed, practised), flags Blind Spots, attaches Atlas notes, and suggests next steps.

functions.suggest: Picks up to three next steps: re-check Blind Spots, train waiting Workouts on risky files, explore the folder with most unpractised complex files, or drill one.
functions.practiceByFile: The latest practice outcome per source file and the Workout kinds used on it, from Attempts and from outcomes recorded before Attempts existed.
functions.buildMap: Builds the map: scores tracked files, marks the repository's most complex quarter red when unpractised, practised files amber once their code changed enough, and AI-changed ones amber.
functions.groupByDirectory: Groups file entries by folder, counting states and Blind Spots, giving each folder its worst state, and sorting files worst first.
functions.changedSince: How many lines of a file were added or removed since a commit, used to tell when practice has gone out of date.

src/synthesis/generate.ts.text: Generates and saves one Workout or a Series of Predictions: runs synthesis with progress messages, saves what was Verified, and records every paid token in the spend ledger.

functions.describeEvent: Turns a generation event (generating, verifying, rejected with feedback) into a progress line naming the attempt.
functions.generateWorkout: Generates a Workout from a target, saving it with its cost and context once Verified, and records the spend even when generation fails midway.
functions.generateSeries: Generates a Series of Predictions about one unit and saves each question with its share of the cost and its place in the Series.

src/synthesis/prompt.ts.text: The instructions the model follows for each Workout kind, and the user prompt carrying the numbered source plus any commit, What-if, Track step, or business rule.

functions.kataSystemPrompt: Rules for a Kata: extract a self-contained unit, remove one contiguous piece of its logic behind a wrong-value placeholder, and write a brief, tests, and two hints.
functions.drillSystemPrompt: Rules for a Drill: extract a self-contained unit, inject one realistic bug in at most 3 lines, and write symptom-only tests, an incident report, and two hints.
functions.predictionSystemPrompt: Rules for a Prediction: a plain-English Scenario with four measured outcomes, wrong ones as Variants, with extra rules for commit Predictions and What-ifs.
functions.drillUserPrompt: The request for one Workout: the numbered source, what to build it around (a symbol, commit, or What-if), plus any Track step and business rule to ask about.
functions.diagnosisSystemPrompt: Rules for a Diagnosis: a practice incident and four plausible Causes, each a Variant whose test shows its Symptom, so only knowing the system picks the right one.

src/synthesis/schema.ts.text: The shapes the model must return for each Workout kind and the checks run before verifying: required fields, Variants, no code names shown to non-coders, no spoilers.

functions.predictionProblems: Checks a Prediction: four options with one correct, an old or today option for commit or What-if ones, valid Variants, and no code names in what non-coders read.
functions.seriesOverlaps: Finds Series questions that repeat another's Scenario, true outcome, or Variant, so each question tests a different misunderstanding.
functions.ruleProblems: Checks a rule check: it names which option the rule predicts with a note, and neither Scenario nor options quote the rule and give the answer away.
functions.checkWorkoutOutput: Lists everything wrong with a generated Workout before running it: slug, time, source anchors, Quick limits, hints, spoilers, and the kind-specific checks.
functions.diagnosisProblems: Checks a Diagnosis: four Causes with one correct, each with its own symptom, test, and a Variant that occurs exactly once in the healthy code.

src/synthesis/synthesize.ts.text: The generate-check-verify loop: asks the model, checks the answer's shape, runs the Verified Gate in the sandbox, and feeds problems back until it passes or attempts run out.

functions.synthesizeSeries: Generates a Series of Predictions, keeping each question that is Verified and asking only for the missing ones until the Series is complete.
functions.synthesizeDrill: Generates one Workout, retrying with feedback from schema checks or the Verified Gate, and stops early when the file isn't worth practising.
functions.generate: One model call for structured output; a malformed answer is kept with its error and billed usage so the retry can fix it, while other failures stop generation.

src/workouts/debrief.ts.text: The Debrief after a Workout: where the code lives, what it is for, the business flows it runs in, rules it may enforce, who calls it, computed tensions, and neighbours to try next.

functions.renderDebriefText: Writes the Debrief for the terminal, section by section, with the Try next commands aligned.
functions.renderDebriefMarkdown: Writes the Debrief as a Markdown document titled after the Workout.
functions.buildDebrief: Gathers the Debrief from the Atlas, links, rules, and flows: target functions, callers, blast radius, churn, hidden coupling, and up to a few next Workouts as commands.
functions.findTarget: Works out which real functions a Workout is about, from where its versions differ, else from its named symbol and source anchors.
functions.calling: Says which of the target's functions the files using it call, more briefly when every user calls the same one.

src/workouts/rulechecks.ts.text: What rule checks have found: each rule's latest answered verdict, checks still waiting for an answer, which went stale as the code changed, and which commits should trigger a new one.

functions.changedSinceCheck: Says why a rule check is out of date: its file or function is gone, the function changed since, or the file changed by enough lines.
functions.commitRuleTriggers: Finds the rules whose checked or pinned function a commit changed, ranking rules that held before first, so the commit gets a rule check.
functions.bodyAt: A function's body at a given revision, whitespace-trimmed, so two versions can be compared.
functions.ruleChecksWaiting: The rules whose newest rule check is generated but not yet answered.
functions.ruleChecks: Each rule's latest answered rule check: whether the code followed it, where it was checked, and whether it has gone stale.

src/workouts/save.ts.text: Saves a Verified Workout to the workspace: its record and provenance, code and test files, and a README per kind, with Around this code, Track, What-if, and rule context.

functions.newSeriesId: A unique dated id for a new Series of Predictions, numbered when the name is already taken.
functions.sourceRevision: The commit a Workout's source comes from and whether the file has uncommitted changes.
functions.rulePlacement: Records a rule check's verdict: which option the rule predicts, whether the code follows it, or whether the rule describes the code before the commit.
functions.uniqueId: A Workout id not used by any current or finished Workout, numbered when the base is taken.
functions.trackPlacement: The README line saying which Track a Workout belongs to and why its file matters.
